subject: physics
question_text: What is banking of roads? Derive an expression for the angle of banking of a curved road.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: What banking is
lines: A vehicle on a curve needs a force towards
the centre. Raising the outer edge of the
road above the inner edge is called banking.
The tilted normal force then supplies that
force, so friction is not relied on.
steps.why: Friction changes with rain, dust and worn tyres; a banked road works from geometry alone, which is why the design does not depend on the weather.
common_mistakes: Saying the road is banked "to reduce friction" — it is banked so that friction is not needed.

recall.must_convey: That banking means raising the outer edge so the tilted normal force supplies the centre-directed force.
accept: tilted normal force supplies the force
reject: N sin theta equals m v squared by r

steps.label: The two equations
lines: For a smooth road banked at an angle θ, the
horizontal part of N turns the vehicle and
the vertical part carries its weight:

lines.text: N sin θ = m v² / r

steps.why: Splitting one force into its sideways part and its upward part is the whole method; dividing then removes N, which we never wanted.
common_mistakes: Swapping sine and cosine, which puts the weight on the horizontal equation.

recall.must_convey: That N sin theta equals m v squared by r and N cos theta equals m g.
accept: N sin theta equals m v squared by r
N cos theta equals m g

steps.label: The result
lines: Dividing the first equation by the second,
The mass cancels, so one banking angle suits
a light car and a loaded truck alike.
steps.why: The angle is fixed by the speed the road is designed for, which is why a sharp curve carries a speed limit sign.
common_mistakes: Leaving m in the answer, or writing tan θ = rg/v² upside down.

recall.must_convey: That tan theta equals v squared by r g, with the mass cancelling.
accept: tan theta equals v squared by r g
reject: N cos theta equals m g
